history.summary: IMPORTANT - NOT the famous Deshnoke (Bikaner) rat temple: this is a distinct, genuine Karni Mata shrine in Udaipur, so the CSV row is valid and must not be conflated with the Deshnoke temple (any seq 861 entry for Deshnoke would be a separate shrine). The Shri Manshapurna Karni Mata Temple stands atop the Machla Magra Hills near Doodh Talai Lake, close to the centre of Udaipur city, enshrining a stone idol of Karni Mata. Travel sources date it to 1620-1628 under Maharana Karan Singh of Mewar (verify). 'Manshapurna' means wish-fulfilling, reflecting the belief that the goddess grants devotees' wishes. It is reached by Rajasthan's first ropeway (built 2008, from Deendayal Upadhyay Park at Doodh Talai) or by a pedestrian-only stepped path; the hilltop gives panoramic views of Udaipur's lakes, City Palace and the Aravallis, and is a popular sunset point. Some sacred rats (kabas) are kept here, but it is not the Deshnoke-scale phenomenon.
